findings.claim: Drift re-approval of gate_implement bypasses implementation_ready, including evidence freshness and pending convergence.
findings.evidence: _approve_drift calls required_gate_artifact, trace_precondition and review_precondition at lines 12842–12849, then writes an approved decision. It never calls implementation_ready or gate_precondition_hook. cmd_gate_approve dispatches directly to this path whenever drift_queue is nonempty (lines 12620–12622). Thus a fresh PASS review of a rebuilt manifest can re-approve while the last converge still owes tasks, and evidence checks are also bypassed.
findings.suggested_fix: Use implementation_ready for gate_implement in _approve_drift before any approval, baseline or audit write; test pending convergence and stale/failing evidence through drift re-approval.

findings.claim: Removing a mapped test can evade test_expectation_change because vanished mappings remain in the historical verification record.
findings.evidence: _mapped_test_names selects the latest historical row per criterion and unions its evidence.tests, without checking evidenceId freshness. cmd_verification_map appends rows only for criteria present in the new report (lines 15926–15940). If the only mapped test for a criterion disappears, no replacement row is appended, so _mapped_test_names still returns that deleted test. cmd_loop_record compares these historical sets at lines 16631–16636; with unmapped passes allowed, the loop can report ready_for_gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare complete test-case inventories captured from each iteration's JUnit report, bound to its evidence, rather than historical disposition rows. Cover disappearance of the sole mapped test and disappearance of an unmapped test.

findings.claim: Changing an acceptance-tagged test's assertion while preserving its name never triggers the required human stop.
findings.evidence: cmd_loop_record detects test expectation changes only through deleted file paths and shrinking mapped-name sets (lines 16630–16636 and 16651–16658). There is no comparison of modified tagged tests or assertions. PLAN §4.3 explicitly requires stopping when an ACC-tagged test is removed or changed; a weakened assertion with the same test name and a passing run reaches the 'elif not unmet' ready_for_gate branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture acceptance-tagged test content at the run baseline and stop for human disposition when those tests change expected behavior; conservatively stop on tagged-test edits where semantic equivalence cannot be established.

findings.claim: The progress digest can stop a repairing loop despite its failing-test set improving.
findings.evidence: _loop_progress returns 'tests': [tests.get('status'), tests.get('exit_code')] rather than failing test IDs. Two runs that both exit 1 but repair different failing tests therefore have identical test contributions; if obligations and findings stay unchanged, cmd_loop_record reports no_progress. PLAN §4.3 and BRIEF §5 require the set of failing tests in the digest.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist and hash a sorted failing-test identity set from captured results. Define an explicit fallback for runners without structured results rather than treating equal exit codes as equal failures.

findings.claim: Reconcile accepts unticking approved tasks, contrary to the one-way mutation policy.
findings.evidence: The checkbox comparison normalizes both lines to '[ ]' and accepts any checkbox-only difference. A read-only Python probe of _tasks_delta('- [X] T001 done\n', '- [ ] T001 done\n') returned ({'ticked': 1, 'appendedSections': []}, None). PLAN §4.4 explicitly permits only '- [ ]' to '[X]'/'[x]'. The accepted reverse change is then audited and rebaselined as a tick.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the original task checkbox to be unchecked and the new checkbox to be checked; reject reverse transitions and add direct and command-level tests.

findings.claim: A crash after reconcile writes the loop record but before saving state leaves task baselines unrecoverable through reconcile.
findings.evidence: cmd_tasks_reconcile replaces run.tasksSnapshot and records the reconcile step, then write_loop_record at line 16592, append_audit and save_state at lines 16593–16600. A crash before save_state leaves the disk artifact_shas at the previous tasks digest while the loop snapshot and step have advanced. Retrying reconcile is refused by _step_order_ok, and starting another run refuses tasks_drift against the old gate baseline.
findings.suggested_fix: Make reconciliation recoverable with a persisted transaction containing old/new baselines and an idempotent recovery path, so restart can complete the state/audit update without duplicating steps or requiring gate re-approval.

findings.claim: Manifest and review writers do not enforce the approved active-loop ordering, allowing duplicate evidence production during resume.
findings.evidence: PLAN §4.1 states that 'manifest build, artifact review and tasks reconcile consult the active loop step and refuse out of order.' cmd_manifest_build reads state and runs tests without consulting read_loop_record or _step_order_ok. The AS-25 test repeats only 'loop step --step manifest'; it does not retry manifest build itself. Rebuilding outside the recorder is merely detected later by _check_tree_unmoved, after another evidence file has already been produced.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the active loop's permitted output-producing step before manifest builds and implementation reviews, with an explicit stale-recovery exception and idempotent resume behavior.

findings.claim: The missing-mapped-test test is vacuous and the classification test never exercises ambiguity.
findings.evidence: test_a_mapped_test_that_disappears_stops_the_loop asserts 'first.data["stopReason"] == "ready_for_gate" or True' and ends without removing a test or running a second iteration. test_a_stated_environment_blocker_or_ambiguity_ends_the_run returns inside the first loop iteration at line 428, so requirement_ambiguity is never tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the unconditional assertion with a two-iteration test that removes a previously mapped test and requires test_expectation_change. Parameterize classification cases with independent fixtures so both environment_blocker and ambiguity execute.

findings.claim: The R2 submodule fix still omits symlink entries inside submodules, allowing implementation changes without invalidating evidence.
findings.evidence: The top-level tree walk hashes symlinks as 'link:' plus their targets (lines 18694–18695), but the new submodule walk explicitly skips '_is_link(inner)' at line 18707. Retargeting or deleting a tracked symlink inside a gitlink directory therefore leaves the digest unchanged, although the same change outside a submodule invalidates evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Include submodule symlink entries using the same link-target hashing as top-level entries; add tests for retargeting, adding and deleting a tracked submodule symlink.
